title: Dynamic headroom predictor + token-aware admission gating for sustained high-QPS
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Under prolonged high QPS bursts our serving nodes experience cascading degradation: microbatch sizes collapse, KV cache eviction churn increases, and GPU memory headroom oscillates causing transient OOMs and request failures. Existing admission controllers are reactive (based on queue depth or instantaneous GPU free mem) and do not account for token-length distributions or short-term QPS momentum.

Goal: Build a predictive, token-aware headroom estimator and an admission gating policy that combines: (1) short-horizon QPS momentum prediction, (2) token-length distribution sampling per-route, and (3) KV-prefetch budget accounting — to produce a smooth, soft-backpressure signal that reduces tail latency and prevents memory storms while preserving throughput. The system should integrate with current microbatch allocator and KV slab manager and expose controls in the Console for per-customer and per-model budgets.
acceptance_criteria:
1) In synthetic load tests (40k sustained qps with 50% messages >512 tokens) P99 tail token-latency for hosted tiers should improve by >= 12% compared to current reactive admission baseline.
2) GPU OOM/eviction-related request failures should drop to < 0.1% during sustained bursts.
3) KV cache hot-key hit rate degradation during bursts should be limited to < 5% vs baseline.
4) Feature toggles in Console for headroom tuning must work and respect tenant overrides.
5) Implementation must include end-to-end telemetry (headroom estimate, admission decisions, microbatch sizes) and a rollout plan with canary on 5% traffic before fleet-wide enable.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 - Research & design (1 week): define headroom model inputs and output API. Draft algorithm: EWMA momentum for QPS, weighted token-length quantiles, conservative per-GPU slot reservation, and KV prefetch budget deduction.
Phase 2 - Prototype (2 weeks): implement a lightweight headroom predictor service in the runtime control plane that publishes per-node headroom tokens every 100ms. Integrate a token-aware admission hook in the microbatch allocator that consumes headroom tokens.
Phase 3 - KV integration (1 week): coordinate with KV slab mgr to reserve a small fraction of slabs (configurable) for predicted hot prefixes and deduct reserved bytes from headroom. Add a soft-preempt flag to reduce KV prefetch on pressure.
Phase 4 - Observability & rollout (1 week): add Console charts, alerts, and a canary rollout.
Phase 5 - Post-rollout tuning (2 sprints): collect telemetry, tune EWMA windows and quantile weights, and add per-model presets.
Deliverables: design doc (Confluence), runtime PR, microbench harness, Console UI changes, rollout playbook.
experiments:
1) Compare EWMA window sizes (200ms, 500ms, 1s) for QPS momentum vs. reactive threshold under synthetic sinusoidal bursts.
2) Ablation: with and without token-length weighting to measure impact on microbatch occupancy and P99.
3) KV budget realism test: reserve 2%, 5%, 10% of slab space and measure hit rate vs. memory headroom.
4) Integration test toggles: soft-reject (deferred retry) vs early-reject with 503, measure user-visible error rate vs latency improvements.
Monitoring: run A/B on 5% production traffic (canary) and capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, microbatch size distribution, KV hit rate, GPU free mem percentile, and admission decision rate.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: synced with KV team (Lina), runtime (Diego), and console (Mina). Agreed headroom API should be 100ms publish interval.
2026-03-04 - Design review: opted for EWMA QPS momentum + 90th token-length quantile instead of mean to bias for long tails. Lina requested conservative default KV reserve of 5%.
2026-03-06 - Prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12389 (headroom estimator + basic admission hook). Added unit tests for backpressure transitions.
2026-03-08 - Observability: Mina prototyped Console charts and a per-route toggle. Need telemetry keys finalized before canary. Added TODO to attach runbook for canary rollback.

2026-03-10 - Risk: early-reject may increase client retries and amplify QPS in short windows. Decided to implement exponential backoff hint in 503 response and default to soft-delay for first rollout.
